text:
nora: quick flag  our edge onboarding sample is causing weird TS inference in customers' monorepos. Overloaded SDK functions are resolving to broad any types after bundling with esbuild + isolatedModules.

diego: hmm, do you have the package.json exports/types and a failing tsconfig?

nora: yes. package.json (sdk) snippet:
```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    "./": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
    }
  },
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```

nora: consumer tsconfig (root):
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "esnext",
    "target": "es2020",
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false
  }
}
```

olivia: two things to watch: 1) our .d.ts emitting top-level ambient declarations (declare global) that can collide with lib.dom, and 2) internal helpers using `as any` which cause overload inference to degrade to any in the emitted declarations.

sam: yup. TS will pick the package.json "types" regardless of import/require conditionals, so if that umbrella d.ts contains global augmentations it leaks. Also esbuild transforms used in edge dev flow generate different import patterns that can change how module augmentations are attached.

diego: short fixes:
- make all distributed types module-scoped (no bare declare global). use `declare module '@redwood-inference/sdk' {}` augmentations instead.
- remove `as any` from helpers; replace with `unknown` plus explicit typed overloads so d.ts preserves generics.
- split type outputs per entrypoint and use conditional types in package.json: "types": { "import": "dist/esm/index.d.ts", "require": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts" }.

olivia: and add a small consumer test in CI that bundles with esbuild + isolatedModules then runs tsc typecheck to replicate the exact dev flow users hit on Vercel Edge. Right now we only run tsc on the library sources which misses bundler-induced issues.

sam: also add a lint rule forbidding top-level `declare global` or any d.ts that doesn't `export {}` at the top level. That prevents accidental globals in future builds.

types-bot: types CI  branch fix/edge-types-scope (job #213)  failure: "TS2300 Duplicate identifier 'Document'" traced to dist/types/global-augment.d.ts.

nora: i'll open a PR that scopes augmentations, splits d.ts per entry, and scrubs `as any` usage. i'll include a minimal reproducer and the esbuild consumer test.

diego: when you open it, add a short SDK migration note about conditional types and the reason for the change so customers on older TS see the rationale.

olivia: also update the onboarding sample README to mention a temporary workaround: set `skipLibCheck: true` in consumer tsconfig when using the sample app on edge until the fix lands.

sam: small follow-up: watch for overload signatures that rely on inferred generics from rest parameters. those are especially fragile when helpers are untyped. Prefer explicit generic parameters on exported overloads.

nora: thanks  i'll ping internal support with the repro so we can help the affected customer. PR incoming.
